topics.name: Baseline assessment
subtopics: Weeks 1-2 are allocated to baseline assessment alongside the content listed for these weeks

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Counting (integrated with number patterns and mental maths)
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 0 and 180 (weeks 1-4) and 200 (weeks 5-6, 9-10)
Count forwards and backwards in 10s, 5s, 2s, 3s and 4s from any multiple between 0-80 (weeks 1-2), 0-180 (weeks 3-4) and 0-200 (weeks 5-10), and in 100s to at least 500
Use the relationship between + and -; emphasise more than, less than; ascending and descending order

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Mental maths (number range 200)
subtopics: Order a given set of numbers; compare numbers to 150 (weeks 1-4) and 200 (weeks 5-10) and say which is 1-5 or 10 more or less
Rapid recall of addition and subtraction facts to 15 (weeks 1-4) and 20 (weeks 5-10)
Add or subtract multiples of 10 from 0-100
Strategies: put the big number first to count on or back, number line, doubling or halving, build up or break down

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 200
subtopics: Count out concrete objects to 180 (weeks 1-2), 190 (weeks 3-4) and 200 (weeks 5-10); estimate and check by counting reliably; group counting

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols up to 500
Write number symbols and number names to 250

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 99
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers to 80 (weeks 1-2) and 99 (weeks 5-6, 9-10): smaller than, greater than, >, <, =
Describe and order numbers from smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest (weeks 1-4, 7-8)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value (numbers to 99)
subtopics: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of tens and ones up to 80 (weeks 1-2) and 99 (weeks 5-6, 9-10); use flard cards / place value cards daily
Identify and know the value of each digit

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context up to 99
subtopics: Addition and subtraction (weeks 1-2, 5-6, 9-10)
Repeated addition leading to multiplication (weeks 3-10); equal grouping and sharing leading to division that may include remainders (weeks 3-4, 9-10)
Sharing leading to fractions (weeks 5-8)
Money problems involving totals and change (weeks 1-2, 5-8)
Techniques: building up and breaking down, doubling and halving, number lines, rounding off in tens (CAPS pp. 79-80 problem types)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 99
subtopics: Addition and subtraction to 80 (weeks 1-4) and 99 (weeks 5-10) using +, -, = and □; practise number bonds to 20
Multiply numbers 1 to 10 by 2 and 5 (weeks 1-2) and by 2, 5, 3, 4 (weeks 3-8) using ×, □, =
Divide numbers to 50 by 2, 5, 10 using ÷, □, = (weeks 3-8)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Fractions
subtopics: Use and name unitary fractions 1/2, 1/4, 1/3, 1/5
Recognise fractions in diagrammatic form; write as 1 half, 1 third, 1 quarter

topics.name: Measurement: Telling time
subtopics: Read dates on calendars; place birthdays, public events and holidays on calendars
Tell 12-hour time in hours, half hours and quarter hours, minutes on analogue and digital clocks

topics.name: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric patterns (integrated with 3D objects)
subtopics: Copy, extend and describe simple patterns made of physical objects, drawings, shapes
Range of patterns: simple patterns in which shapes or groups of shapes are repeated in the same way
Create and describe own patterns

topics.name: Space and shape: 3D objects and position
subtopics: Range of 3D objects: boxes, balls, cylinders
Features of objects: straight sides, round sides, roll, slide
Language of position: in front of, next to, inside

topics.name: Measurement: Length
subtopics: Estimate, measure, compare and record length using non-standard measures (hand spans, paces); describe length in informal units
Language of comparison: longer, shorter, taller, wider
Introduce formal measuring: metre sticks, metre lengths of string; estimate and measure lengths in centimetres using a ruler

topics.name: Data handling: Collect, represent and analyse data
subtopics: Collect data about the class or school
Represent data in tables and bar graphs
Analyse data from representations provided

topics.name: Remediation
subtopics: Supporting learning gaps: reteach using another strategy for improved learning; record findings where further support is required

topics.name: Consolidation
subtopics: Reinforce more of the same (practice) to embed knowledge and skills; give learners the opportunity to ask questions

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Repeat the knowledge and skills taught to establish whether learning has taken place, before new concepts are taught

sba: One formal assessment task (FAT) per term
Weeks 5-6: Space and shape; Patterns, functions and algebra (practical); Numbers, operations and relationships (written)
Weeks 7-8: Measurement (written and oral); Numbers, operations and relationships; Data handling (written)
